newsitem.title: USA: U.S House Speaker Gingrich urges faster GDP growth.
newsitem.headline: U.S House Speaker Gingrich urges faster GDP growth.

text.p: U.S. House Speaker Newt Gingrich said on Friday that Congress would seek advice from Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan on how to raise U.S. economic growth to a range of four to five percent.

In his first public appearance since returning from a 10-day trip to Asia, Gingrich told business supporters that the United States should try to emulate the economic vitality of South Korea, Taiwan, and Hong Kong by establishing four percent annual real growth as a minimum.
Gingrich called last Tuesday's Federal Reserve interest rate hike "unconscionable" because the action would seek to undermine economic growth to quell inflation.

"We will be asking Alan Greenspan to submit to the Congress what changes he thinks are necessary in the American system so that he would feel comfortable at the Fed sustaining four- to five- percent real growth," Gingrich said.
"Our goal should be to say bluntly upfront: we want the high-growth, high-income, high-take-home-pay, high-opportunity society. And we're not going to settle for anything less," Gingrich said.

Gingrich said that Greenspan, were he speaking in his previous role as a private-sector economist, would favor Republican legislative goals like abolishing the capital gains tax, eliminating many regulations on business and reforming litigation law.
"It is unconscionable to have the Federal Reserve system close off economic growth because of some theoretical model," he said.
